questions.stem: How does data consolidation differ from data virtualization and data federation?
options: It is restricted to relational databases
It keeps complete historical copies of data from all source systems
It never uses ETL or ELT
It creates only virtual views over the sources
It exposes data through a single query language
questions.explanation: Virtualization and federation host no copy of data, whereas data consolidation keeps complete historical copies of all the data coming from all the source systems.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a data consolidation environment?
questions.explanation: Data warehouses, data marts, data lakes, delta lakes, data vaults and business vaults all fall under the umbrella of data consolidation environments.

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT fall under the umbrella of data consolidation?
questions.explanation: Data federation hosts no copy of data, so it is not a consolidation environment; the other four keep physical copies.

questions.stem: What processing sometimes takes place during data consolidation?
options: A complex ETL or ELT to process data into different data models
Real-time write-back into the source systems
Conversion of relational data into web services
questions.explanation: In consolidation, sometimes a complex ETL or ELT processes data into different data models, and sometimes a one-to-one data model is maintained.

questions.stem: Data virtualization, data federation and data consolidation are discussed together with respect to what?
questions.explanation: All three are discussed together as approaches to exposing data to data consumers.

questions.stem: Besides transforming data into different models, what other data model approach can a consolidation environment maintain?
options: A one-to-one data model with the source
questions.explanation: Sometimes a one-to-one data model is maintained in the consolidation environment rather than a transformed one.

questions.stem: Which of these approaches hosts no copy of data in its own environment?
questions.explanation: Data federation, like data virtualization, does not host any copy of data; the others are consolidation environments that keep physical copies.

questions.stem: Under which umbrella do data vaults and business vaults fall?
questions.explanation: Data vaults and business vaults are named among the data stores that fall under the umbrella of data consolidation environments.

questions.stem: What is the scope of the copies kept in a data consolidation environment?
options: Only the latest snapshot of each source
Complete historical copies of all data from all source systems
Only data that has passed quality checks
questions.explanation: Data consolidation keeps complete historical copies of all the data coming from all the source systems.

questions.stem: Which statement about data consolidation is correct?
options: It always requires a complex ETL
It never maintains a one-to-one model
It is a virtual layer without storage
It may use a complex ETL or ELT, or maintain a one-to-one data model
It is limited to data lakes
questions.explanation: Consolidation sometimes involves complex ETL or ELT into different data models and sometimes keeps a one-to-one data model.
